evidence_detail: DOI RESOLVES (true). Handle 10.1016/j.isci.2026.115778 -> linkinghub PII S2589004226011533; Crossref: 'Revolutionary horizons in nonaqueous and aqueous-nonaqueous electrolyte design for safer high-performance zinc-ion batteries', iScience 29(5):115778, published 2026-05 (created 2026-04-17), Sun AY, Simi NL, Pol VG; PMC13156642, PMID 42111170, CC BY-NC 4.0 gold OA. The 2026 date is NOT a placeholder: it is a genuine article indexed by Crossref, PubMed and PMC, and today is 2026-11-23, so it is about six months old. VALUE VERIFIED VERBATIM IN THE DOCUMENT: full text (Europe PMC PMC13156642) Table 3 'Nonaqueous molecule structures and properties in design categories' contains the row 'gamma-valerolactone (GVL) | 36.1 | - | 58 | - | -' under the 'Selected polar aprotics' category, i.e. dielectric constant = 36.1, donor number = '-', single-solvent reference = 58. SOURCE IS NOT PRIMARY (false): this is a PERSPECTIVE/REVIEW. The dataset's own metadata agrees (source_quality=open_access_review_table, evidence_level=open_access_review_table, source_table='Table 3'). The authors performed no permittivity measurement; 36.1 is a compiled literature descriptor whose only citation (ref 58) is Xie C. et al., 'Robust and Wide Temperature-Range Zinc Metal Batteries with Unique Electrolyte and Substrate Design', Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2023;62, doi 10.1002/anie.202304259, i.e. a zinc-battery paper, not a dielectric or thermophysical study. That reference is a secondary carrier at best. TEMPERATURE IS IMPUTED, NOT REPORTED: Table 3 has NO temperature column (header = Category | Solvent | Structure | Dielectric constant | Donor number | single-solvent refs | multi-solvent refs | ANA refs). The strings '298.15' and '25 C' do not occur anywhere in that table; the only '298' occurrences in the whole article are inside reference page numbers. The queue's T=298.15 K comes from a default rule, confirmed by dielectric_v04.csv temperature_source='review_table_standard_room_temperature' and gate flag 'temperature_review_table_standard'. So the row asserts a (T, epsilon) pair at a temperature the cited document never states. SYSTEMATIC, NOT ISOLATED: six v04 rows draw on this same Table 3 and reproduce it exactly - v04row-224 DOL 7.3, v04row-225 THF 7.5, v04row-236 NMP 32.2, v04row-243 TEP 13, v04row-244 TMP 21.6, v04row-227 GVL 36.1 - all matching the Table 3 cells I read, all stamped T=298.15 K with the same imputation. This is a cluster-level ingestion defect from one open-access review table. INDEPENDENCE: not independent of R248 in any meaningful sense. 36.1 here is a compilation; 36.9 in R248 is a solvent-descriptor table. Neither is a measurement, so the 2.2 percent spread is the ordinary spread between two compilation lineages, very likely both downstream of a common handbook or solvent-table tradition, not a genuine measurement disagreement. LEDGER ABSENCE IS NOT THE NBS-514 MECHANISM: the 135-row coverage gap registry splits cleanly into 102 NBS514_CIRCULAR_MANUAL_ENTRY rows (ingestion_path=literature_manual_entry, a legitimate manual-transcription class) and 33 UNFLAGGED_NO_OBSERVATION rows with ingestion_path='unknown'. v04row-227 is in the 33-row 'unknown' class, NOT the NBS class. Its gate_flags are empty; the source layer (2065 rows, 61 ThermoML documents) contains 0 gamma-valerolactone rows and does not list this DOI among its 61 source_document_ids, and source_document_registry_v1.csv (61 entries) omits it too. INGESTION IS EXPLICITLY UNVERIFIABLE: the row is a ThermoML-absent value entered from a review table with no declared ingestion path, so 'PROVENANCE_INCOMPLETE / NO_CONTRIBUTING_MEASUREMENTS' is the correct machine verdict and the row cannot be reconstructed from the source layer. NUMERICALLY the value is not implausible (gamma-butyrolactone about 39, GVL slightly lower), so the defect is provenance, not magnitude. DECISION: HOLD. The document and the number are real and quotable, but the row is a tertiary compiled value with an imputed temperature, so it cannot serve as the primary leg of a same-T conflict. Do NOT average with R248. Route to the primary document.

DOI RESOLVES (true). Handle 10.1016/j.ica.2021.120372 -> linkinghub PII S0020169321001286; Crossref: 'Experimental and theoretical investigation of the cycloisomerization of N-propargylcarboxamide catalyzed by NHC-Au-X in green solvents', Inorganica Chimica Acta 522:120372, July 2021, Segato J, Baratta W, Belanzoni P, Belpassi L, Del Zotto A, Zuccaccia D. DOI and citation are real and well formed. THE JOURNAL CHOICE IS DEFENSIBLE BUT GVL'S ROLE IS NOT: Inorg. Chim. Acta is a legitimate venue for gold-NHC catalysis, and the published abstract confirms gamma-valerolactone really is one of the screened solvents ('most of these solvents (cyclohexanone, isopropyl acetate, MIBK, ethyl lactate, furfuryl alcohol, gamma-valerolactone, propylene carbonate and propionic acid) are comparable or better solvents with respect to traditional VOS'). So GVL genuinely appears in this paper - but as a REACTION SOLVENT in a catalysis study, not as a characterised dielectric material. NO EVIDENCE THE PAPER MEASURES PERMITTIVITY: the record points to 'supporting information' as the page; a static epsilon in such an SI table is normally a cited solvent descriptor used to rationalise solvent polarity, not a value these authors measured. The 113 Crossref reference entries contain no dielectric, permittivity, handbook, CRC, Landolt or Wohlfarth item, so the SI table cannot be shown to be a primary measurement; it is at least as likely a compilation. VALUE CANNOT BE VERIFIED: the article is closed access (Unpaywall oa_status='closed', is_oa=false), has no OA copy, and is absent from Europe PMC (hitCount 0 for this DOI). No PDF, SI or page image for this DOI exists anywhere in the repository (searched 115778, 120372, ica.2021, isci, and all PDFs). PROVENANCE CHAIN IS CORRUPT AT ITS ORIGIN: the dielectric_v04.csv notes record that the upstream was a Reaxys queue row carrying NO DOI, and that the queue row mislabelled the compound's InChIKey as JYVATQXCHBTGRN-UHFFFAOYSA-N (not GVL). The DOI was back-resolved through Crossref afterwards; it was never read off a document the project possesses. A post-hoc DOI attribution to an unseen SI is exactly the case where 'DOI resolves' must not be read as 'value is sourced'. TEMPERATURE IS IMPUTED HERE TOO: dielectric_v04.csv temperature_source='not_reported' and gate flag 'temperature_not_reported'; T=298.15 K was imputed by the same room-temperature default as R227. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE CONFLICT ITSELF: the premise - same compound, same T=298.15 K, two different epsilon - is not supported. NEITHER leg states 298.15 K. The two rows were placed at a common temperature by an imputation rule, and only then compared. INDEPENDENCE: the pair is not two independent measurements. R227 is a review-table compilation citing a battery paper; R248 is a solvent-properties descriptor in a catalysis SI. Both are almost certainly derived from a shared handbook or compilation lineage, so an independence-based resolution (AVERAGE_JUSTIFIED, or picking one as 'the measurement') would be unsound. LEDGER ABSENCE: same class as R227 - v04row-248 sits in the 33-row ingestion_path='unknown' group of the coverage gap registry, not in the 102-row NBS514_CIRCULAR_MANUAL_ENTRY group, so this is NOT a legitimate manual transcription of a printed handbook. DECISION: FAIL as an evidence row in its current state - not because the DOI is fake (it is real) but because the record asserts an unverified epsilon at an unreported temperature, attributed post hoc to an SI the project has never retrieved, from an upstream row that carried the wrong structure key. evidence_grade=INSUFFICIENT. Do NOT average with R227.
